property_summary: For all callers, only the admin (the deployer) can change C.owner via setOwner; the mutant removes that restriction allowing some non-admin caller to change owner and thus violate the rule.

For all callers, setOwner can only be successfully invoked when the caller is the original admin (the deployer); the mutant that checks owner instead of admin allows the current owner to call setOwner and so can change owner when called by a non-admin owner.

For any admin-invoked setOwner call that does not revert, the reference contract always returns true; the mutant returns false for some inputs, so there exists an input where the return value differs (false) — the test asserts the call succeeded and returned true.

For any admin-chosen new owner address, setOwner always returns true after a successful call in the reference implementation; the mutant sometimes returns false (specifically when the returned expression compares the input to the previous owner), so there exist inputs where the mutant's return value differs.

For any caller and any address _owner passed by the admin, the reference setOwner always returns true after a successful call; the mutant can return false for some inputs (specifically when the returned value incorrectly compares the new owner to the previous owner), so there exist fuzzed _owner values that make the mutant's return differ from true.

For any address _owner set by the admin, C.setOwner succeeds and returns true; the mutant may return false when the returned expression wrongly compares the new owner to the previous owner, so there exists an _owner that makes the mutant return false while the reference returns true.

For any address newOwner supplied by the admin caller, calling setOwner(newOwner) succeeds and causes the public owner getter to equal newOwner; the mutant still sets owner but can return a differing boolean for some newOwner values, so we assert the observable owner equals the provided newOwner (which the reference always ensures, but the mutant does too — this by itself won't distinguish), therefore instead we assert that the return value of setOwner (captured via a try/catch call) is true whenever the call succeeds; the reference always returns true, while the mutant can return false for some inputs, so this property holds for the reference for all inputs and is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any admin-invoked setOwner(address), the call completes (does not revert) and the returned boolean is true; the mutant can complete yet return false when the returned expression mistakenly compares the new owner to the previous owner.

For every caller address, calling setOwner(...) on the reference contract either always reverts for non-admins (so only the admin can successfully change owner and the call returns true) while the mutant that removes the onlyAdmin check allows non-admin callers to successfully call setOwner and change owner; thus the general rule: only the admin can call setOwner successfully in the reference, but the mutant lets other addresses succeed.

For every call to setOwner by the admin, the reference contract returns true and also updates the owner to the provided address; the mutant returns true but may not update owner (it can return early), so there exists an input where the returned success is true but owner was not changed.
